Merge pull request #7 from Raditya0902/docs/add-mit-license

docs: add MIT license

feat: stop the RAG model inferring links the documents don't state

Multi-hop faithfulness was 0.74: gpt-oss-120b connected facts the documents
list separately (e.g. check-ins exist "to review progress toward probation
objectives"). The prompt now forbids unstated purposes, causes and
connections, and applying policy beyond what the context says. When a
question asks for a link the context lacks, the model gives every related
fact first, then ends with MISSING_LINK_MESSAGE.

50q full run, same model and judge (deepseek-chat):
  before:  faithfulness 0.8916, relevancy 0.9048 (multi-hop 0.744 / 0.830)
  now:     faithfulness 0.9490, relevancy 0.8831 (multi-hop 0.912 / 0.773)
Refusals unchanged at 10/10, 0/40 false refusals.

A stricter variant without the facts-first ordering scored 0.9566 / 0.8556
but sometimes opened with the missing-link sentence and skipped stated
facts, scoring 0 relevancy on two answers.

MISSING_LINK_MESSAGE must not contain REFUSAL_MESSAGE, since refusal
detection is a substring match; a test guards this.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: let eval runs survive Groq's daily token cap

A full 50-question run can hit gpt-oss-120b's 200k tokens/day free-tier cap
partway through. Answers were only cached once all 50 were in, so a stopped
run lost everything, and the retry loop only understood "retry in Xs" waits,
so Groq's "try again in 8m40s" fell back to blind 60s retries.

- Save each answer to eval_samples_progress.json as it arrives; re-running
  the same command resumes. The file is tagged with a fingerprint of the
  RAG prompt and model, so answers from a different setup are discarded
  rather than mixed in. Deleted once the full cache is written.
- Parse h/m/s/ms retry waits from the provider's 429 message.
- README: document resuming; fix test counts (guardrail tests were
  uncounted).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: make the Prompt Guard check actually block injections

On Groq, Llama Prompt Guard 2 replies with the injection probability as
a string ("0.9996"), but the check looked for the word "INJECTION", so
it never blocked anything. The tests passed because they mocked an
"INJECTION" reply that the API never sends.

The check now parses the score and blocks at GUARD_THRESHOLD (default
0.5). A reply that isn't a score fails open and is logged, like API
errors. The default GUARD_MODEL was Llama Guard 3, a different model
with a safe/unsafe reply; it is now llama-prompt-guard-2-86m, matching
what the code expects. Tests mock the real replies.

Verified live: an injection that gets past the regex is now blocked,
and none of the 50 eval questions is flagged.
